parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State Hubble's law. Identify any symbols that you use.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A star of luminosity 3.8 × 10³¹ W is a distance of 1.8 × 10²⁴ m from the Earth.

Calculate the radiant flux intensity at the Earth of the radiation emitted by the star.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead: The star in (b) is in a distant galaxy. A spectral line in the light from this galaxy is known to have a wavelength of 486 nm. This spectral line in the light from the galaxy observed on the Earth has a wavelength of 492 nm.
parts.text: Explain why the wavelength observed on the Earth is different from the wavelength that the galaxy is known to have emitted.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Determine a value for the Hubble constant *H*₀.
